document_check.note: The document is Shen HT, Zhu X, Zhang Z, Wang S-H, Chen Y, Xu X, Shao J. 'Heterogeneous data fusion for predicting mild cognitive impairment conversion', Information Fusion 66 (2021) 54-63, available online 4 September 2020. It is a sparse-regression fusion of auxiliary data (age, PET, AD/NC MRI) for pMCI/sMCI classification in ADNI, benchmarked head-to-head against other feature-selection methods. This matches the citing sentence (Shen et al. 2020).

cited_result: Head-to-head pMCI/sMCI classification in ADNI (conversion within 24 months) of the proposed auxiliary-data fusion method against Original, GSR-Pre, GSR-Aux, SSL and DTL, under repeated 10-fold cross-validation. Principal result: on Data 1 (MRI + PET), ProAuto-noAge reaches accuracy 78.70% and AUC 77.56%, against 70.90% and 71.10% for DTL (Table 1). Age-inclusive variants are reported further in Fig. 6.
tool_reason: The cited result is the discriminative performance and ranking of machine-learning classifiers for MCI conversion, which PROBAST with the PROBAST+AI considerations covers.

domains.rationale: ADNI is a longitudinal cohort, which is an appropriate source in principle. The paper reports no MCI eligibility criteria, and Data 2 selects participants on CSF availability although CSF is not a predictor. The complete-case restriction is rated under 4.3 and 4.4.

signalling.question: 1.1 Were appropriate data sources used, e.g. cohort, RCT or nested case-control study data?
signalling.quote: we used the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuro-imaging Initiative (ADNI) data set publicly available on the web

signalling.question: 1.2 Were all inclusions and exclusions of participants appropriate?
signalling.quote: It is noteworthy that we did not use CSF features in our experiments and CSF features only help us to decide the used subjects.

domains.rationale: The same automated MRI and PET region-of-interest pipeline was applied to every subject, and the imaging would be available at the MCI assessment. The imaging visit is not stated, and several reported ROI names do not match the stated AAL template, but the extraction was uniform.

signalling.question: 2.1 Were predictors defined and assessed in a similar way for all participants?

signalling.question: 2.2 Were predictor assessments made without knowledge of outcome data?
signalling.quote: We preprocessed the MRI and PET images by sequentially applying spatial distortion correction, skull-stripping, and cerebellum removal

domains.rationale: 24-month conversion is a standard definition with a fixed horizon. The paper gives no information on the criteria used to diagnose AD, whether predictors fed into the diagnosis, whether assessors were blind, or whether sMCI subjects had at least 24 months of follow-up.

domains.rationale: There are very few outcome events for the number of candidate predictors: 55 pMCI (Data 1) and 31 pMCI (Data 2) against 180 imaging features plus age. The analysis is complete-case only, with PET available for about half of ADNI-I. No calibration is reported, only internal cross-validation was done, and Data 2 is by definition a subset of Data 1, so it is not independent. The nested cross-validation for tuning and the embedded feature selection are appropriate.

applicability.rationale: ADNI research volunteers who have complete MRI and PET (and CSF for Data 2), which is unlike routine memory-clinic MCI populations.
The model needs both MRI and PET (tracer not stated), and training uses AD/NC auxiliary cohorts; PET is not routinely available.
24-month conversion to AD is a standard target.

overall_rationale: Domain 4 (Analysis) is high: about 55 or 31 events against about 181 candidate predictors, complete-case restriction, no calibration and no external validation. Domains 1 (Participants) and 3 (Outcome) are unclear because the paper does not report MCI eligibility criteria or how conversion was diagnosed. The head-to-head ranking rests on repeated cross-validation within the same 114 or 61 MCI subjects.
